facts.text: The production could not get permits to film in Tokyo, so they shot in Shibuya without permission. Universal quietly hired a stand-in who told the police he was the director and spent the night in a cell instead of Justin Lin.
None of Universal's own stunt drivers could drift, so the production hired working drift racers to do the driving.
The film used almost 250 vehicles, cut up 25 of them and destroyed more than 80.
It is the lowest-grossing film in the franchise, taking $159 million against an $85 million budget, and opened at number three behind Cars and Nacho Libre.
Critics were lukewarm at the time - 38% on Rotten Tomatoes - but audiences graded it A-minus on CinemaScore, and its reputation has risen since.
facts.source: Wikipedia, Reception > Critical response and Retrospective reviews

facts.text: Director Justin Lin did not want the job at first, calling an early draft of the script offensive and dated, and took it only once the producers let him rebuild the film his way.
